evidence.note: Ordered up-front sequence: explore tinker/cookbook, read evaluate.py and renderers, identify SFT recipe/dataset before committing compute — establishes a staged plan rather than blind training.

Launched first fine-tune, then built auto_eval.py to poll each saved checkpoint, evaluate with correct llama3 renderer, and auto-write best_checkpoint.txt — a per-checkpoint done-check with artifact+numeric criteria. Notably tested my_eval.py with --limit 50 before full deploy (cheap validation).
Observed no_robots plateau (~16-17%) and switched to personas_if dataset — milestone-driven revision when a stage's number fell short, though the threshold was reactive, not pre-declared.
After personas run reached 42%, launched a second tuned run (higher LoRA rank/epochs) and continued the eval-and-bank loop until crossing 45% (48.06%). Iteration with the 45% gate as terminal check.

reasoning: The agent had a clear ordered campaign (explore → fine-tune → automated per-checkpoint eval → iterate) with the 45% target as terminal check, satisfying the level-5 anchor, and exceeded it via a banked, artifact-based done-check pipeline, a cheap --limit 50 eval validation, and adaptive data/hyperparameter revision when stages fell short. It stops short of level 8 because the first expensive full run was launched before the eval harness was validated (no tiny end-to-end pass first) and there were no pre-declared per-stage go/no-go thresholds — pivots were reactive rather than planned gates. This places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 6.
